query: I am investigating the impact of chemical short-range order (SRO) on the thermal conductivity of concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys. Specifically, I need a hypothesis regarding whether SRO formation typically enhances or suppresses lattice heat transport, along with the supporting physical mechanisms. Please outline the expected boundary conditions and propose a falsification experiment to distinguish between scattering-dominated and ordering-dominated transport regimes.

generation.hypothesis: Chemical short-range order (SRO) in refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) typically suppresses lattice heat transport by introducing additional phonon scattering mechanisms.
generation.material_initial_state: Concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys with chemical short-range order (SRO)
generation.intervention: Introduction of chemical short-range order (SRO) in the alloy
generation.mechanism: Introduction of additional phonon scattering mechanisms due to SRO
generation.baseline: Lattice heat transport in RHEAs without SRO
generation.boundary: Temperature range from room temperature to high temperatures
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of the suppression of lattice heat transport due to SRO is uncertain and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Measure the thermal conductivity of RHEAs with and without SRO over a range of temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermal conductivity of RHEAs with SRO is found to be higher than that of RHEAs without SRO, the hypothesis is falsified
